newsitem.title: USA: Md. firm gets approval for Va. retirement center.
newsitem.headline: Md. firm gets approval for Va. retirement center.

text.p: Senior Campus Living said Wednesday it won zoning approval from Fairfax County, Va., to develop a $321 million continuing care retirement community in Springfield, Va.
SCL, based in Catonsville, Md., said it will begin contruction of the 2,100 resident campus, named Greenspring Village, next Spring.
The financing for the project was arranged through Equitable Real Estate Investment Management Inc of New York. No bonds will be used, according to a spokesman for the SCL, Mel Tansill.
The facility is expected to employ more than 1,000 people and generate more than $1 million in property taxes for Fairfax County, SCL said.
SCL currently manages Charlestown and Oak Crest Village retirement communities in Maryland, and the Henry Ford Village community in Michigan.
Tansill said SCL plans to have facilities for 20,000 retirees by the year 2000, up from the 4,000 at the three sites now run by the company.
